evidence: Specific: the content structure belongs to this centre and its rules - 20-minute slot tiles with 'Few left'/'Full' tags, rules stated beside controls ('Rubble (up to four bags)', 'Starts DRC-, then five digits', 'Slots last 20 minutes; the last slot starts at 17:20'), permit field appearing only for Van, done page built around the gate reference DR-204117.

Generic: the visual layer is a stock public-sector form kit - white bordered cards on pale grey, one green filled button, bold sans headings, underlined text links, numbered step text; swapping 'recycling centre' for a library room booking or a GP slot would need no visual change.
The only identity marks are the council name in bold text and a small bin outline icon in the masthead (root/default/375-light, all routes).

unfinished: No focal point at the first viewport of 'when': title, intro, step text and day buttons all carry similar weight; the slot grid is the only visual mass (root/default/375-light).
Identity is only the council name in body-weight bold text plus a 16px bin icon; no colour or typographic moment carries the council.
Done page at 1440 is two bordered boxes and an outline button; the page ends above the fold and the footer band stops short, leaving an empty grey band below it (done/default/1440-light).
Slot grid stops at ~816px while the 'Opening days' card below spans the full 1088px column, so bands of the 'when' page end at different right edges for no reason (root/slot-chosen/1280-light).
The vehicle info button (circled i) is stranded on its own row under the vehicle choices at 375 (vehicle/van/375-dark).
Headings differ from body mainly in size and weight; 'Slots', 'Morning', 'Afternoon' and the unlabelled 'Few left' group read as a document outline rather than a designed schedule.
evidence: Clean, orderly and legible at 375 and 1280, light and dark, with a firm 4px-radius bordered system - nothing broken or clashing.

But nothing is worth looking at beyond the form itself: no drawn device, no use of the council green beyond buttons and selected states, and the confirmation page (the screen a resident will show at the gate) is bare text in boxes.
For an Operate surface this plainness is close to correct; it falls short of 'plain, not bare' mainly on the done page and the 'when' page's lack of a focal point.
